marking_points.text: Identifies the column mass as m = ρAh

option_feedback.A: Correct. The volume is Ah, so m = ρV = ρAh.
option_feedback.B: Dividing area by height does not give the column volume.
option_feedback.C: Density multiplies volume when m = ρV; it does not divide it.
option_feedback.D: ρgh has the units of pressure, not mass.

questions.unit_policy: No unit is requested in this conceptual MCQ.

marking_points.text: Explains that column weight and base area scale together, so A cancels in pressure

option_feedback.A: A static liquid still has weight; static means its acceleration is zero.
option_feedback.B: The derivation works for any chosen area A, not only 1 m².
option_feedback.C: Correct. A larger column has proportionally more weight spread over proportionally more area.
option_feedback.D: Pressure is force divided by area, not force multiplied by area.

option_feedback.A: Correct. Δh is the vertical separation between the two levels.

questions.answer: V = Ah and ρ = m/V give m = ρAh. The liquid weight is W = mg = ρAhg. The pressure difference due to this column is Δp = F/A = W/A = ρAhg/A = ρgh. One valid assumption is that the liquid is static or that its density is uniform.
accepted_alternatives: Use p for the surface-to-base pressure difference if it is explicitly described as the pressure due to the liquid column.
questions.unit_policy: A symbolic derivation needs no numerical unit, but any stated unit for pressure must be Pa or N m⁻².
questions.tolerance: Accept algebraically equivalent sequences that explicitly use both controlled definitions and W = mg.

marking_points.text: Uses V = Ah with ρ = m/V to obtain m = ρAh
Uses W = mg to obtain the liquid-column weight ρAhg
Uses pressure as force divided by area and cancels A to obtain Δp = ρgh
States a valid assumption that the liquid is static or has uniform density

questions.answer: The lower face has upward pressure force p₂A. The upper face has downward pressure force p₁A, and the slab weight ρAΔhg is also downward. Equilibrium gives p₂A = p₁A + ρAΔhg, so p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh. A cancels because all three forces are proportional to the same chosen area.
accepted_alternatives: A correctly labelled force diagram may replace the verbal force statements.
questions.unit_policy: A symbolic derivation needs no numerical unit. Pressure difference would have unit Pa.
questions.tolerance: Accept an equivalent zero-resultant-force equation with a consistent sign convention.

marking_points.text: Identifies p₂A upward at the lower face and p₁A downward at the upper face
Identifies the slab weight ρAΔhg acting downward
Uses equilibrium and rearranges to p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh
Explains that all forces scale with the same area A, which therefore cancels

questions.answer: For a slab of area A between the levels, p₂A upward balances p₁A + ρAΔhg downward. Therefore p₂ - p₁ = ρgΔh. Δp = 860 × 9.81 × 0.75 = 6327.45 Pa = 6.33 × 10³ Pa. From p = F/A, F = ΔpA = 6327.45 × 2.40 × 10⁻³ = 15.2 N. The resultant force is from the higher-pressure side toward the lower-pressure side.
accepted_alternatives: Accept 6.3 × 10³ Pa and 15 N to two significant figures if working is consistent.
questions.unit_policy: Pressure difference requires Pa or N m⁻². Resultant force requires N.
questions.tolerance: Accept Δp from 6.32 × 10³ Pa to 6.34 × 10³ Pa and force from 15.1 N to 15.3 N.
